note: Codes: data/mexico_2025_safety.do (Bookmark #30, Q3 2024 Trust in Government) keeps INEGI columns bp5_1_1, bp5_1_2, bp5_1_3 from conjunto_de_datos_ensu_cb_0924.csv (import delimited case(lower)) and reshapes long with item = column name (core model s3 pattern 1, no positional step); code 9 set missing by the Section V recode ('capture replace bp5_1_* = . if bp5_1_* == 9'). mapping_basis=data_labels: INEGI's Q3 data dictionary labels BP5_1_1 'Confianza en la administracion publica: Gobierno federal', BP5_1_2 '...: Gobierno estatal/Gobierno de la CDMX', BP5_1_3 '...: Gobierno municipal/Gobierno de la alcaldia (CDMX)'; 3/3 agree with questionnaire 5.1 sub-items 1-3. Cross-check (route 9 style): all 3 live item vectors reproduce the raw INEGI Q3 2024 CSV (24096 rows) after dropping code 9 -- 12/12 item x level counts (bp5_1_1 1/2/3/4 = 4721/11532/4118/3463, bp5_1_2 = 2427/11588/5499/4239, bp5_1_3 = 2232/10353/5390/5772); code 9 = 262/343/349; no blanks, so no skip routing; live 71334 rows, 23962 ids (134 respondents with 9 on all three drop out). Q3 vs Q1/Q2/Q4 (checked against each quarter's print, not assumed): Q3 is NOT the Q1 block. Q1 asks 4.1 'En una puntuacion de 0 al 10 ... cuanto confia en...' about three office-holders (Presidente, Gobernador, Presidente municipal) on 0-10, coded bp4_1_*; Q3 moves trust to Seccion V, asks 5.1 'En su opinion, cuanta confianza le genera...' about three governments, on a 4-point confianza/desconfianza scale, coded bp5_1_*; Q2 and Q4 have no trust block (their Seccion IV is Acoso). No Spanish string is shared with batch_674 (Q1), so nothing was reused and all English is fresh. Scale direction is reversed relative to Q1: here 1 = Mucha confianza (most trust) ... 4 = Mucha desconfianza, while Q1's 0 = Nada, 10 = Completamente. Words: section_prompt (5.1 stem) and item_text (sub-items 1-3) are the administered Q3 questionnaire wording; all 9 shipped Spanish strings found verbatim in the p.7 text layer and checked against a 150 dpi render. Kept as printed: trailing '?', '(CDMX)' (printed non-bold in item 3), the stem's '...'. Stripped: question/sub-item numbers, dot leaders, |__| entry boxes, interviewer direction 'REGISTRE EL CODIGO CORRESPONDIENTE A CADA OPCION', and the closing CP5 script that follows on the same page. Structure: one section (_1), stem in section_prompt, government level in item_text; instructions blank -- Section V has no read-aloud introduction. Options: 1-4 printed 'Mucha confianza' / 'Algo de confianza' / 'Algo de desconfianza' / 'Mucha desconfianza', identical in all three catalogos (the render's wider gap in 'Mucha  desconfianza' is justification, shipped with one space); 9 'No sabe / no responde' has no row (set missing by the .do). Every level each item's respondents used has an option row. Step 3b: live items match question 5.1 exactly (3 items, resp 1-4); dictionary Description ('Public trust in government institutions to address security concerns, Q3 2024') overstates it -- 5.1 asks general trust in three levels of government with no security framing; dictionary Reference names 'ENSU 2023' while data and wording are the 2024 Q3 wave (file suffix 0924) -- same defect as the siblings. INEGI-side oddity, not ours: the Q3 dictionary's PER row gives RANGO_CLAVES '0324' and the raw 0924 CSV's PER column is '0324' in all 24096 rows, although the file, zip and Section V content are Q3. English in _translated is this project's own translation (machine_translation); INEGI publishes no English questionnaire.
public_note: Fuente: INEGI, Encuesta Nacional de Seguridad Pública Urbana (ENSU) 2024, tercer trimestre -- IRW transcribed Section V (question 5.1) from INEGI's questionnaire, stripped interviewer directions, and added an English translation of its own; INEGI does not endorse this item text. Code 1 is the most trust (Mucha confianza) and 4 the least, the reverse of the 0-10 trust item in the 2024 first-quarter table.
